chief_complaint: Post‑myocardial infarction follow‑up with hypertension, metabolic syndrome and lipid management
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 70‑year‑old male with a history of an acute NSTEMI in September 2016, for which he was placed on dual antiplatelet therapy and secondary‑prevention medications. Since then he has persistent stage2 diastolic hypertension (BP 118/95), hyperlipidemia, metabolic syndrome, class I obesity, and mitral valve regurgitation. He also has chronic anemia, pre‑diabetes (A1c 6.4%), and ongoing stress and social isolation. His last recorded clinical encounter was in October 2018; recent labs lack BMI, eGFR, and lipid panel values. He is on multiple cardiovascular agents including aspirin, prasugrel, metoprolol, two statins, and a thiazide diuretic, but no ACE‑I/ARB is documented.

active_problems.name: Localized primary osteoarthritis of the hand

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include prior sinusitis (resolved 2018), acute infective cystitis (resolved 2017), gingival disease (resolved 2017), a resolved myocardial infarction episode (2016), prior medication review and stress episodes, and limited social contact. Chronic background conditions include osteoarthritis of the hand and a lifelong history of higher education.
social_determinants: Full‑time employment at age 70 indicates functional capacity; however, the patient reports social isolation and recent stress. He has a criminal record and holds a higher education degree. No documented tobacco or alcohol use.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular: High risk for recurrent ischemic heart disease, heart failure, stroke, and peripheral arterial disease due to prior NSTEMI, uncontrolled hypertension, hyperlipidemia, metabolic syndrome, obesity, and ongoing dual antiplatelet therapy. Renal: Potential risk for chronic kidney disease given long‑standing hypertension, diuretic use, and anemia, but eGFR is missing. Metabolic: Elevated risk of progression to type 2 diabetes (prediabetes, metabolic syndrome, obesity). Hematologic: Chronic anemia may be multifactorial and could worsen myocardial oxygen delivery. Neurologic: Age and vascular risk factors place the patient at increased risk for stroke and possibly vascular cognitive impairment.

data_quality_flags.issue: BMI value missing; obesity flag present but exact BMI not recorded.
Renal function (eGFR/creatinine) not available, limiting CKD assessment.
Lipid panel values missing; cannot assess adequacy of statin therapy.
